findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable file path aborts the entire program with a panic instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed error such as LoadError::Io

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on fallible parse of external input
findings.failure_mode: A non-numeric second CSV field panics at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error the caller can report to the user
findings.fix: Use .map_err(|e| LoadError::InvalidValue) or similar to return a typed parse error from the Result chain

findings.failure_mode: A u32 value greater than 65535 silently truncates to u16, corrupting the data silently with no error indication to the caller
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| LoadError::ValueOutOfRange) or parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[0] on a collected Vec from split
findings.failure_mode: If a line has zero comma-separated fields (empty line), parts[0] will panic with index-out-of-bounds. Even if lines are non-empty, empty string name is accepted without validation
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and .ok_or(LoadError::InvalidLine) to fail gracefully; validate the name is non-empty

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[1] — accessing second CSV field without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with only one field (no comma) produces a Vec with length 1; parts[1] panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Replace split+collect with split_once(',') and use .ok_or(LoadError::InvalidLine) to return a typed error when the field is missing

findings.problem: Hidden I/O: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) inside the parsing closure
findings.failure_mode: Logging (side effect) is fused into the data-parsing pipeline, violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation. This makes the function untestable in isolation and couples pure parsing to console output
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing pipeline. Return parsed Records; let the shell layer handle logging/metrics separately

findings.problem: Record struct uses raw primitives (String, u16) with no parse boundary — callers can construct invalid states directly
findings.failure_mode: No smart constructor or validation means any caller can create a Record with an empty name or any u16 value, bypassing domain invariants. This is a parse-boundary violation
findings.fix: Add a private constructor or named impl fn new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, RecordError> that validates name is non-empty. Consider a name newtype for the domain

findings.problem: Intermediate Vec<String> allocation via .collect() on split + map, instead of using split_once and borrowing
findings.failure_mode: Every line allocates a new Vec of Strings when only two fields are needed. For large files this multiplies allocation pressure and cache misses unnecessarily
findings.fix: Replace split+map+collect with split_once(',') and parse directly from the borrowed string slices; use try_reserve before collecting into the output Vec
